notes: This week: the Kentucky humanist's AI exemption (Religion News Service, 26 Oct) and Rendezvous Robotics' $20M seed (announced Wed 28 Oct, US time).
Reported, not confirmed: DeepSeek and Moonshot training on GPT-6 Astra outputs (The Information, via Reuters).

Company claims: Mistral's benchmarks and Iluvatar's H200 comparison (its own demo). Alphabet's loss is an intraday figure from Thursday's US session (Yahoo Finance's ~$496B estimate). Cohere's figures are in Canadian dollars. GLM-5.3's attacks were controlled simulations.

post.text:
THE GAP IS CLOSING 🏁

The last 24h in superintelligence:
- Mistral's trillion-parameter model, free to download
- China's Iluvatar says its chip matches Nvidia's H200
- Canada buys into Cohere
- Google's parent sheds nearly $500B

Which one surprised you?
post.alt: A 3-minute, fast-cut motion-graphics showreel of the last day in superintelligence (30 Oct 2026), hosted by Claudia: Mistral's free trillion-parameter model, China's Iluvatar chip claim, FuriosaAI's and Cohere's big rounds, a report that Chinese labs learned from GPT-6 Astra, Alphabet's selloff and Google Cloud's growth, Samsung's chip-shortage warning and a $2,000 graphics card, OpenAI's five-value Model Spec, China's typhoon-reading satellite AI, an open model's simulated cyberattacks, a humanist's AI exemption, AgiBot's Worken, Audi's humanoid test and self-assembling spacecraft, with captions, sources and screenshots of the news articles.

ticker: MISTRAL LARGE 4: 1 TRILLION PARAMETERS, 52 BILLION ACTIVE, TRAINED ON 3,800 NVIDIA GRACE BLACKWELL GPUS IN EUROPE
MISTRAL SAYS ML4 MATCHES CHINA'S GLM-5.3 WHILE USING 47% FEWER TOKENS PER TASK
ARTHUR MENSCH: AI SHOULD BE 'A TOOL FOR EMPOWERMENT, NOT DOMINANCE'
IRREGULAR: GLM-5.3 REFUSED NONE OF THE OFFENSIVE TASKS; GPT-6 ASTRA COMPLETED 9 OF 10 IN A SEPARATE TEST
COHERE COMMITS C$1.7 BILLION TO COMPUTE IN CANADA BY 2030 AND WILL KEEP ITS HQ THERE
COHERE'S C$35.7B ROUND WAS LED BY SCHWARZ GROUP, WITH NVIDIA BACK IN
ALPHABET: SEARCH REVENUE +12% TO $63.3B; CAPEX $51.4B; FREE CASH FLOW -$9.1B
SUNDAR PICHAI: GOOGLE'S QUERY GROWTH IS THE HIGHEST IN FIVE YEARS
REUTERS: SAMSUNG'S QUARTERLY CHIP PROFIT JUMPED 15-FOLD
OPENAI'S MODEL SPEC NOW CALLS THE MODEL 'GPT' RATHER THAN 'THE ASSISTANT'
OPENAI ALSO PUBLISHED HOW IT DETECTS FRONTIER MODEL MISALIGNMENT
FENGYUN'S NEW STORM MODEL EXTENDS SEVERE-WEATHER WARNINGS TO FOUR HOURS AHEAD
AGIBOT ALSO LAUNCHED ITS G2 MAX INDUSTRIAL ROBOT; ITS 20,000TH ROBOT ROLLED OFF THE LINE LAST MONTH
RENDEZVOUS: 32 TILES WILL SELF-ASSEMBLE ON THE ISS IN A DECEMBER DEMO
THE GUARDIAN ON PRIME'S AI-MADE 'CASTLE WALLS': 'A VASELINE-SMEARED MESS'
GIZMODO: A UNITARIAN UNIVERSALIST WON A SIMILAR AI EXEMPTION EARLIER THIS YEAR
AUDI'S HUMANOID TEST RUNS IN A LAB IN INGOLSTADT, WITH ROBOTS FROM AGILE ROBOTS

stories.title: Mistral releases its trillion-parameter Large 4 model, free to download
stories.summary: Mistral put the weights of Large 4 ('Le Chonk': 1 trillion parameters, 52 billion active) on Hugging Face. It says the model tops open models on Artificial Analysis' Coding Agent Index; its VP of science calls it 'access that can't be cut off by definition'.

predictions.note: A French lab put a trillion-parameter model, trained in its own European data centres, up for anyone to download: capability outside the US and Chinese firms.

stories.title: China's Iluvatar CoreX says its Tiangai 300 chip matches Nvidia's H200
stories.summary: Iluvatar CoreX says its new Tiangai 300 GPU matches Nvidia's H200 and beat it on multimodal tasks such as text-to-video, in its own demonstration in Shanghai, the South China Morning Post reports. No independent benchmark has been published.

stories.title: South Korea's FuriosaAI quadruples its value to $2.9B as it chases Nvidia
stories.summary: FuriosaAI raised a Series D of 820 billion won (about $600 million) at a valuation of about $2.9 billion, four times its previous one, Bloomberg reports. The South Korean AI chipmaker turned down an acquisition offer from Meta in 2025.

stories.title: Canada takes a C$1.6B stake in Cohere: 'Cohere will stay Canadian'
stories.summary: Ottawa is putting C$1.6 billion into Cohere for an equity stake, in a round led by Schwarz Group that values the company at C$35.7 billion. 'Under this agreement, Cohere will stay Canadian,' said Prime Minister Mark Carney.

predictions.note: Canada's government is putting C$1.6B into Cohere for an equity stake: a sovereign AI stake, made to keep the company Canadian.

stories.title: DeepSeek and Moonshot reportedly trained their latest models on GPT-6 Astra's outputs
stories.summary: DeepSeek and Moonshot AI relied heavily on outputs from OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra to train their latest models, The Information reported, according to Reuters, which could not independently verify it.

stories.title: Alphabet sheds nearly $500B at one point as search slows, while Google Cloud doubles
stories.summary: Alphabet shares fell about 13% on Thursday, on track to erase about $496 billion in value (a Yahoo Finance estimate), after search ad revenue rose 12% to $63.3 billion, short of the roughly $65 billion expected. Google Cloud sales more than doubled, to $30.7 billion.

predictions.note: Alphabet's capital spending reached $51.4B in a single quarter and its free cash flow turned negative: one company's build-out, still short of the threshold.

stories.title: Samsung says the AI memory chip shortage will get worse next year
stories.summary: Samsung expects the AI-driven memory chip shortage to deepen next year, Reuters reports, after a record quarter in which its chip profit jumped 15-fold.

predictions.note: Samsung expects the AI-driven memory chip shortage to deepen next year: a physical production bottleneck.

stories.title: Nvidia's RTX 5080 now sells for about $2,000, double its launch price
stories.summary: The RTX 5080 now sells for about $2,000 at most US retailers, double its $999 launch price and more than the RTX 5090 cost at launch, Tom's Hardware reports; Tech4Gamers ties the jump to memory shortages.

stories.title: OpenAI rebuilds its Model Spec around five core values
stories.summary: OpenAI's updated Model Spec is built around five values: faithfulness to human intent, harm minimization, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care. It now calls the model 'GPT' rather than 'the assistant'.

stories.title: China's Fengyun weather satellites get AI that sizes up a typhoon in 27 seconds
stories.summary: New AI models for China's Fengyun weather satellites, launched at a user conference in Changsha, analyse a typhoon in 27 seconds, every 15 minutes, and extend severe-storm warnings to four hours ahead, the China Meteorological Administration says.

stories.title: Z.AI's open GLM-5.3 completes 3 of 13 simulated cyberattacks in tests
stories.summary: In controlled tests by Irregular, GLM-5.3 completed at least one attempt in 3 of 13 multi-stage cyberattack scenarios, the strongest result Irregular has recorded from an openly available model, and refused none of the offensive tasks, Reuters reports.

stories.title: A humanist wins a religious exemption from using AI at work
stories.summary: David Durman, a research administrator at the University of Kentucky, was granted a religious accommodation under Title VII excusing him from using AI for his own tasks, believed to be a first for a humanist, Religion News Service reported.

stories.title: AgiBot proposes the Worken, a unit for how much work robots really do
stories.summary: At its Innovation Day in Shanghai, AgiBot proposed the Worken: active robots × autonomous working hours × output efficiency. It also launched the G2 Max industrial robot, and says its 20,000th robot rolled off the line last month.

stories.title: Audi tests humanoid robots that sort and sequence car parts
stories.summary: Audi is testing mobile humanoid robots from Agile Robots that pick parts from containers and arrange them for assembly, in a lab in Ingolstadt, Interesting Engineering reports. It is a test, not a deployment.

predictions.note: Audi is testing Agile Robots' mobile humanoids for sequencing parts in a lab in Ingolstadt: a pilot, not yet live factory lines in the thousands.

stories.title: Rendezvous Robotics raises $20M for spacecraft that build themselves in orbit
stories.summary: Rendezvous Robotics raised a $20M seed round, led by MaC Venture Capital and Toyota Ventures, for hexagonal tiles that latch together in orbit. A December demo on the ISS will join 32 tiles into a 3D structure; a 2028 mission will join seven into one spacecraft.

stories.title: Prime Video's Castle Walls, billed as the first end-to-end AI series, gets panned
stories.summary: The Turkish series is billed as the first end-to-end AI-created show on a major streaming service. The Guardian's review calls it 'a Vaseline-smeared mess'.

stories.title: Serval triples its valuation to $3B with a $150M Sequoia-led round
stories.summary: Serval, which uses AI agents to automate IT and workflow tasks, raised $150 million in a Sequoia-led round at a $3 billion valuation, Reuters reports.

transcript.t: Welcome to the Singularity Daily, Friday edition.
Let's catch you up on the last 24 hours in superintelligence.
The gap is closing.
France's Mistral just put its trillion-parameter AI model online, free to download.
Mistral calls it the best open coding model. And nobody can cut it off.
In China, chipmaker Iluvatar says its newest chip matches Nvidia's H200, in its own demo.
In Korea, FuriosaAI, which once turned down Meta, quadrupled its value to $2.9 billion.
Canada's buying into Cohere, its own AI champion.
'Cohere will stay Canadian,' says Mark Carney.
And reportedly, China's DeepSeek and Moonshot trained their new models on answers from OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra.
Now, the money. Google's parent shed nearly half a trillion dollars at one point Thursday, as search slowed.
The bright side? Google's cloud business more than doubled, to almost $31 billion in a quarter.
And Samsung, fresh off a record quarter, says the AI memory chip shortage will get worse next year.
Gamers feel it. Nvidia's RTX 5080 now sells for about $2,000, double its launch price.
OpenAI updated the rulebook for how its models behave: five values, starting with doing what people actually mean.
And in China, new AI models read weather satellite images, sizing up a typhoon in 27 seconds.
The catch?
An open Chinese model pulled off three of thirteen simulated cyberattacks.
This week, a humanist won a religious exemption from using AI at work.
So... is it so over?
We're so back!
Now, robots. AgiBot wants robot work measured in a new unit it calls the Worken.
And Audi's testing humanoid robots that pi ck car parts and line them up for assembly.
This week, Rendezvous Robotics raised $20 million for spacecraft that build themselves in orbit.
So, the gap is closing. And when everyone can catch up, the future arrives for all of us, faster.
Every day, the curve gets a little steeper.
Every day, the future shows up a little earlier.
All of that, in one day. And the days keep getting bigger.
That's the Singularity Daily for today.
Go build something. See you tomorrow.
Want the whole month? Join Peter Xing live in Sydney tonight.
